# Start here

For a developer, or an AI assistant, opening this repository for the first time.
Read this and you will know enough to make a change without breaking something
subtle.

## What this is

Clip is a macOS menu-bar clipboard manager, written in Swift and SwiftUI, with
no third-party dependencies.
<!-- COUNTS:START (generated by docs/generate-counts.py - do not hand-edit) -->
**~51,433 lines of Swift** across 138 files, **2,062 behaviour-assertion call sites** in `qa-probe.py`, **47 security-check call sites** in `security-probe.py`.
<!-- COUNTS:END -->
It keeps what you copy,
recognises what kind of thing it is, and holds a small library of reusable text
(prompts, notes, skills, design documents, colors).

## Get it running in five minutes

```bash
./build.sh
```

That builds and launches it. Look in the **menu bar** - there is no Dock icon
and no window until you press ⌘⇧Space. Grant Accessibility when asked, or the
global shortcut and pasting will not work.

## Then run the tests, before you change anything

```bash
xcodebuild -project Clip.xcodeproj -scheme Clip -configuration Testing \
  -derivedDataPath build-testing CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build

CLIP_QA=1 CLIP_QA_SANDBOX=1 CLIP_HEADLESS=1 \
  ./build-testing/Build/Products/Testing/Clip.app/Contents/MacOS/Clip &

python3 qa-probe.py         # expect: all passed, 0 failed - it prints "N passed, N failed, N skipped"
python3 security-probe.py   # expect: all passed, 0 failed
```

If those are green before you start, anything red afterwards is yours. That is
worth thirty seconds every time.

## The six things to know before touching the code

**1. The Xcode project is generated.** Add a `.swift` file anywhere under
`Clip/`, then `python3 regen-project.py`. Never hand-edit the pbxproj.

**2. Nothing expensive goes on the capture path.** Copying happens hundreds of
times a day and must stay instant, offline and free. No model call, no network
request, no full-library scan in `ClipboardMonitor` or `HistoryStore.add`.

**3. `visibleItems` is memoised, and the cache key must be complete.** If you
add an input to `computeVisibleItems`, add it to `DerivationKey` in the same
commit, or the list will silently go stale. `derivationAudit` catches this if
you run it.

**4. Tests run sandboxed, always.** `CLIP_QA_SANDBOX=1` moves the database,
media, Keychain and preferences aside. Without it you will damage real data;
this has happened twice.

**5. Measure before you optimise.** `perf-probe.py --save before`, change one
thing, `--compare before`. Reading the code has pointed at the wrong bottleneck
every time so far.

**6. A silent guard is a defect, even when the code is right.** This is the
rule, and it is where new code should head: a `guard … else { return }` or
`try?` on a user-triggered or startup path should succeed, fix the problem
itself, or report through `NoticeCenter` (transient / persistent / integrity)
with a sentence from `StorageDiagnosis` or `AIDiagnosis`.

What is actually enforced today is narrower. Section 134 of the probe
(`run_m4_silent_paths`, printed as "134. NO SILENT GUARDS") audits a named
list of 15 functions - the ones one lane's work touched - and fails the suite
if a new, unallowlisted silent guard appears in one of those 15. The Swift
tree has well over 1,000 function declarations in total; the other ~1,100 or
so, including roughly 155 `try?` sites and several hundred
`guard ... else { return }` sites, are not covered by this gate; they may or
may not report through `NoticeCenter` today. Widening the
gate to the rest of the codebase is planned, not done - see the function's
own docstring in `qa-probe.py` for exactly which 15 and why. Until then, read
"the suite enforces no silent guards" as "the suite enforces no *new* silent
guards in these 15 functions", not as a codebase-wide guarantee.

The Diagnostics window (menu-bar icon, Settings > Privacy) shows every open
notice and the activity log; the Startup Health check
(`Core/StartupHealth.swift`) runs before anything touches data and writes a
backup before every migration.

## Where to look for what

| I want to change... | Look in |
|---|---|
| How a copy is captured or classified | `Core/ClipboardMonitor.swift`, `Core/ItemClassifier.swift` |
| What the list shows, filtering, search ranking | `Core/HistoryStore.swift` |
| Storage, migrations, versions | `Core/Database.swift`, `Core/Migration.swift` |
| Sync, tokens, Google sign-in | `Core/SyncManager.swift`, `SyncClient.swift`, `GoogleAuth.swift` |
| AI actions and providers | `Core/AIService.swift`, `Core/AIProvider.swift` |
| Colors, themes, the contrast audit | `Theme/` |
| The panel, cards, editors | `Views/` |
| Settings | `Views/Settings*Pane.swift`, `Views/SettingsShell.swift` |
| The test harness | `Core/QABridge.swift`, `qa-probe.py` |

`ARCHITECTURE.md` explains how these fit together and why several of them are
shaped the way they are. It is worth twenty minutes.

## A prompt, if you are pointing an AI assistant at this

> This is Clip, a macOS menu-bar clipboard manager in Swift/SwiftUI with no
> third-party dependencies. Read `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` and
> `CONTRIBUTING.md` before proposing anything.
>
> Rules this codebase holds to, which override your defaults:
>
> - Nothing expensive on the capture path. Copying stays instant and offline.
> - Measure before optimising, and re-measure after. `perf-probe.py` exists for
>   this. Reading the code has picked the wrong bottleneck every time.
> - Every assertion must be proved able to fail: break the code deliberately,
>   watch it go red, put it back. `--prove` runs the ones that must fail.
> - Tests never touch real data. Always `CLIP_QA_SANDBOX=1`.
> - Comments explain *why*, usually including what went wrong first. Match that.
> - When a test fails after a deliberate design change, update the assertion to
>   the new intent. Do not relax it and do not work around it.
> - The app stores every password its user has ever copied. Treat anything
>   touching the pasteboard, the database, the Keychain or the network as
>   security-relevant, and add a check to `security-probe.py`.
>
> Before you finish: run `qa-probe.py` and `security-probe.py` to completion
> and report the actual "N passed, N failed, N skipped" line each one prints,
> rather than asserting success.

## Good first changes

- A new item kind in `ItemKind` plus its detection in `ItemClassifier`.
- A new AI action, following the shape of an existing one in `AIService` - note
  that it must be suggestion-then-diff-then-confirm like every other one.
- A new built-in theme in `AppTheme.presets`. It has to pass the 43-pairing
  audit, and `auditThemes` will tell you if it does not.
- Broadening a detector: `SkillDetector` and `DesignDocDetector` are both
  forgiving parsers of documents written by humans and by several different
  models, and they can always recognise more.
